Anvil storm-top — a wide flat-topped mass of dark-bley and grey cotton-elements spread across the upper sky-baseplate, the base hanging low, a built thunderhead frozen in structure.

Thin coastal sea-haze — trans-clear and trans-white tiles scattered across the lower distance behind coastal rock-plates, the far headlands faded into pale brick-suggestion, a gentle static obscurity.
Midday blue-clarity — sky-baseplate in solid medium-blue, no cotton or round-plates added, just sharp brick-edges on every peak and slope, an unfiltered high-noon mountain atmosphere.

Deep winter grey — a thick uniform layer of dark-grey and light-bley round-plates blanketing the full sky-zone, the peaks barely differentiated below, a heavy monochrome brick atmosphere.

Pre-dawn murk — a deep dark-bley sky-baseplate with a thin seam of trans-clear tiles at the horizon edge, the mountains below a dark silhouette, a static built moment before first light.

Twilight zenith-fade — a gradient from dark-bley plates at the top of the sky-baseplate down to trans-clear tiles at the horizon band, the range silhouetted below, a built static dusk-sky depth.

Smoke-haze from valley floor — trans-grey and trans-clear tiles layered at low altitude across the valley-plate, upper peaks untouched, the built suggestion of still-air valley smoke, muted and quiet.

Snowstorm ceiling — a solid packed layer of white round-plates and cotton-elements replacing the entire upper sky-baseplate, only the nearest foreground slope-bricks visible below, a static white-out built in brick.
